claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B.

claims.claim: mRNA in situ hybridisation revealed abundant Lats2 transcripts upon conditional deletion of Lats1, suggesting a compensatory upregulation of Lats2 in the absence of LATS1.
claims.source: mRNA in situ hybridisation against Lats2 at P2, revealed abundant Lats2 transcripts upon conditional deletion of Lats1, suggesting a compensatory upregulation of Lats2 in the absence of LATS1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C), similar to previous reports of elevated YAP/TAZ signalling inducing Lats2 expression (Moroishi et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Deletion of Lats2 alone (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats2fl/fl) did not reveal any developmental morphological anomalies.
claims.source: To overcome potential functional redundancy, we deleted both Lats1 and Lats2 in RP. Deletion of Lats2 alone (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats2fl/fl), did not reveal any developmental morphological anomalies (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D) and pups were identified at normal Mendelian proportions (Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and breeding data in Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: Deletion of any three out of four Lats alleles did not affect pituitary development and were identified at normal ratios.
claims.source: Similarly, deletion of any three out of four Lats alleles did not affect pituitary development and were identified at normal ratios, similar to other tissues (Lavado et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by breeding data and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Homozygous Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants were identified at embryonic stages at reduced Mendelian ratios and were absent at P0-P2, suggesting embryonic and perinatal lethality.
claims.source: Homozygous Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants were identified at embryonic stages at reduced Mendelian ratios and were absent at P0-P2, suggesting embryonic and perinatal lethality (Supplementary file 2).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by breeding data presented in Supplementary file 2.

claims.claim: Haematoxylin/eosin staining of the developing pituitary gland in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants revealed overgrowth of RP by 13.5dpc compared to controls (n = 4).
claims.source: Haematoxylin/eosin staining of the developing pituitary gland in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants revealed overgrowth of RP by 13.5dpc compared to controls lacking Cre (Figure 2A, n = 4).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Total TAZ and YAP proteins accumulated throughout the developing gland in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl double mutants at 13.5dpc.
claims.source: Total TAZ and YAP proteins accumulated throughout the developing gland in double mutants (arrowheads) but only in the SOX2+ periluminal epithelium of controls (arrows).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The same regions in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants showed a marked reduction in pYAP-S127 staining at 13.5dpc.
claims.source: The same regions showed a marked reduction in pYAP-S127 staining, which is observed in SOX2+ cells of the control (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: LATS1/2 normally regulate YAP and TAZ in the pituitary.
claims.source: These findings are in line with LATS1/2 normally regulating YAP and TAZ in the pituitary and demonstrate successful deletion in RP.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the accumulation of YAP/TAZ and loss of pYAP in LATS1/2 mutants.

claims.claim: The Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutant pituitary was highly proliferative at 13.5dpc.
claims.source: The mutant pituitary was highly proliferative (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2F; Ki-67 index average 47.42% ± 1.73 SEM in control versus 76.04% ± 9.11 SEM in the double mutant, p=0.0067, Student's t-test)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Ki-67 immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B and quantified in Figure 2—figure supplement 2F.

claims.claim: The majority of cells in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants expressed SOX2 but not SOX9 at 13.5dpc.
claims.source: and the majority of cells expressed SOX2 (Figure 2A,C) but not SOX9 (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figures 2A-C.

claims.claim: By 15.5dpc the Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutant pituitary was grossly enlarged and exerting a mass effect on the brain, had cysts and displayed areas of necrosis (n = 5).
claims.source: By 15.5dpc the pituitary was grossly enlarged and exerting a mass effect on the brain, had cysts and displayed areas of necrosis (asterisks Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 2E, n = 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 2E.

claims.claim: Staining for Endomucin revealed poor vascularisation in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants compared to controls at 15.5dpc.
claims.source: Staining for Endomucin to mark blood vessels revealed poor vascularisation in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants compared to the ample capillaries seen in the control (Figure 2C), which may account for the necrosis.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Ectopic residual pituitary tissue was frequently observed at more caudal levels in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants, reaching the oral epithelium.
claims.source: We frequently observed ectopic residual pituitary tissue at more caudal levels, reaching the oral epithelium and likely interfering with appropriate fusion of the sphenoid, similar to other phenotypes involving pituitary enlargement (arrows Figure 2C) (Andoniadou et al., 2012; Sajedi et al., 2008; Gaston-Massuet et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C and citations to similar phenotypes.

claims.claim: Immunofluorescence revealed abundant active (non-phosphorylated) YAP throughout the Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutant pituitary at 15.5dpc.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence to detect active (non-phosphorylated) YAP revealed abundant staining throughout the pituitary at 15.5dpc, compared to the control where active YAP localises in the SOX2 epithelium (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: Very few cells expressing PIT1, TPIT and SF1 were observed in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl double mutants at 15.5dpc.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence using specific antibodies against lineage commitment markers PIT1, TPIT and SF1 at 15.5dpc revealed very few cells expressing PIT1, TPIT and SF1 in the double mutant (Figure 2D; PIT1 9.14% in mutants compared with 51.4% in controls (Student's t-test p<0.0001); TPIT 4.0% in mutants compared with 11.4% in controls (Student's t-test p<0.007); SF1 2.1% in mutants compared with 6.5% in controls (Student's t-test p>0.05) n = 3 mutants and five controls), suggesting failure to commit into the three lineages.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2D.

claims.claim: The LATS/YAP/TAZ axis is required for normal embryonic development of the anterior pituitary.
claims.source: These data suggest that the LATS/YAP/TAZ axis is required for normal embryonic development of the anterior pituitary and that LATS1/2 kinases control proliferation of SOX2+ progenitors and their progression into the three committed lineages.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LATS1/2 deletion experiments.

claims.claim: LATS1/2 kinases control proliferation of SOX2+ progenitors and their progression into the three committed lineages.
claims.source: These data suggest that the LATS/YAP/TAZ axis is required for normal embryonic development of the anterior pituitary and that LATS1/2 kinases control proliferation of SOX2+ progenitors and their progression into the three committed lineages.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LATS1/2 deletion experiments showing increased proliferation and reduced commitment.

claims.claim: By P56, all Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl pituitaries examined exhibited lesions of abnormal morphology consisting of overgrowths, densely packed nuclei and loss of normal acinar architecture (n = 15).
claims.source: Postnatal analysis of Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl pituitaries revealed that by P56, despite developing normally during the embryonic period, all glands examined exhibited lesions of abnormal morphology consisting of overgrowths, densely packed nuclei and loss of normal acinar architecture (n = 15).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from postnatal analysis of LATS1 mutants.

claims.claim: Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries developed identifiable lesions accumulating YAP and TAZ at earlier time points (P21 n = 4), the earliest being 10 days.
claims.source: To minimise the likely redundancy by LATS2 seen at embryonic stages, we generated Lats1 mutants additionally haploinsufficient for Lats2 (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+). These pituitaries also developed identifiable lesions accumulating YAP and TAZ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), which were observed at earlier time points (P21 n = 4), the earliest being 10 days, indicating increased severity.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: The number of lesions observed per animal was similar between Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl and Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ models at P56 (3–8 per animal).
claims.source: The number of lesions observed per animal was similar between the two models at P56 (3–8 per animal).
claims.evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the analysis of both models.

claims.claim: Deletion of Lats2 alone (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats2fl/fl) did not result in any defects.
claims.source: Deletion of Lats2 alone (Hesx1Cre/+;Lats2fl/fl), which is barely expressed in the wild type pituitary, did not result in any defects (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Histological examination of Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries confirmed the abnormal lesions were tumours, characterised by frequent mitoses, focal necrosis, and a focal squamous differentiation, as well as the occasional presence of cysts.
claims.source: Histological examination of Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries confirmed the abnormal lesions were tumours, characterised by frequent mitoses, focal necrosis, and a focal squamous differentiation, as well as the occasional presence of cysts (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 3A.

claims.claim: Tumours in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries accumulated YAP/TAZ and upregulated expression of targets Cyr61 and Ctgf.
claims.source: These lesions were identical to those in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl pituitaries (not shown). These tumours accumulated YAP/TAZ and upregulated expression of targets Cyr61 and Ctgf (Figure 3B), confirming the validity of the genetic manipulation (Figure 3B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence and RNAscope data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Analysis of proliferation by Ki-67 immunostaining revealed an elevated mitotic index of 7–28% in tumours (mean 15.46, SEM ±2.74), compared to 2.97% (SEM ±1.2) mean in control pituitaries.
claims.source: Analysis of proliferation by Ki-67 immunostaining revealed an elevated mitotic index of 7–28% in tumours (mean 15.46, SEM ±2.74), compared to 2.97% (SEM ±1.2) mean in control pituitaries not carrying the Lats1 deletion (Figure 3C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantified Ki-67 immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: The tumours in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries were positive for cytokeratins using AE1/AE3 (multiple keratin cocktail).
claims.source: In keeping with the morphological evidence of epithelial differentiation (Figure 3A), the tumours were positive for cytokeratins using AE1/AE3 (multiple keratin cocktail) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: The tumours showed focal morphological evidence of squamous differentiation and showed positive nuclear p63 staining.
claims.source: Furthermore, the tumours showed focal morphological evidence of squamous differentiation and showed positive nuclear p63 staining, frequently expressed in squamous carcinomas (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: The tumours did not show immunohistochemical evidence of adenomas, being negative for neuroendocrine markers synaptophysin and neuron-specific enolase.
claims.source: In contrast, the tumours did not show immunohistochemical evidence of adenomas, that is, they were negative for neuroendocrine markers, which all types of adenomas are typically positive for: the neuroendocrine marker synaptophysin and neuron-specific enolase (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: The lesions were negative for chromogranin A, a neuroendocrine granule marker often expressed in clinically non-functioning pituitary adenomas.
claims.source: The lesions were also negative for chromogranin A, a neuroendocrine granule marker often expressed in clinically non-functioning pituitary adenomas.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: Tumours were negative for vimentin, expressed by spindle cell oncocytoma, an uncommitted posterior pituitary tumour.
claims.source: Tumours were also negative for vimentin, expressed by spindle cell oncocytoma, an uncommitted posterior pituitary tumour (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: Immunostaining against PIT1, TPIT and SF1 showed only sparse positive cells within the lesions, suggesting lack of commitment into endocrine precursors.
claims.source: Moreover, immunostaining against PIT1, TPIT and SF1 showed only sparse positive cells within the lesions, suggesting lack of commitment into endocrine precursors and supporting the undifferentiated nature of the tumour cells (Figure 3D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3D.

claims.claim: Staining for gamma-H2A.X detected elevated DNA damage in cells of the Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mutant pituitaries compared with controls.
claims.source: Consistent with a tumourigenic phenotype, and role for LATS1 genomic stabilisation (Pefani et al., 2014), staining for gamma-H2A.X detected elevated DNA damage in cells of the mutant pituitaries compared with controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and citation to previous work on LATS1 function.

claims.claim: The absence of adenoma or oncocytoma markers together with the histological appearance, observation of focal necrosis and a high mitotic index support the features of squamous carcinoma.
claims.source: The absence of adenoma or oncocytoma markers together with the histological appearance, observation of focal necrosis and a high mitotic index support the features of squamous carcinoma.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined histological and immunohistochemical characterization of the tumours.

claims.claim: Tumour regions in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ pituitaries were mostly composed of SOX2 positive cells (85–97% of cells, 7 tumours across four pituitaries).
claims.source: Tumour regions were mostly composed of SOX2 positive cells, a sub-population of which also expressed SOX9 (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A; 85–97% of cells, 7 tumours across four pituitaries).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: Close examination of the marginal zone epithelium revealed a frequent 'ruffling' resembling crypts in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mutants.
claims.source: Close examination of the marginal zone epithelium, a major SOX2+ stem cell niche of the pituitary, revealed a frequent 'ruffling' resembling crypts, likely generated through over-proliferation of the epithelial stem cell compartment (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by histological and immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: Tamoxifen induction at P5 or P21 in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+;R26mTmG/+ mice led to abnormal lesions in the anterior pituitary within three months in all cases.
claims.source: Tamoxifen induction at P5 or P21, led to abnormal lesions in the anterior pituitary within three months in all cases.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the Sox2-CreERT2 lineage tracing experiments.

claims.claim: All animals with tamoxifen induction at P5 developed lesions by P35 in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+;R26mTmG/+ mice.
claims.source: We focused our analyses on inductions performed at P5, from which time point all animals developed lesions by P35 (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the Sox2-CreERT2 lineage tracing experiments shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice strongly accumulated YAP and TAZ.
claims.source: Similar to observations in Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ animals, these areas strongly accumulated YAP and TAZ (Figure 4B)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice activated expression of targets Cyr61 and Ctgf.
claims.source: activated expression of targets Cyr61 and Ctgf
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice displayed ruffling of the AL epithelium.
claims.source: displayed ruffling of the AL epithelium (Figure 4C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1E)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope and histological data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice lacked lineage commitment markers.
claims.source: and lacked lineage commitment markers (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ mice showed a similar marker profile to Hesx1-Cre-targeted tumours, with positive p63 and AE1/AE3 staining.
claims.source: These lesions showed a similar marker profile to Hesx1-Cre-targeted tumours, with positive p63 and AE1/AE3 staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Lineage tracing confirmed expression of membrane GFP in tumourigenic lesions in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+;R26mTmG/+ mice, suggesting they were solely derived from SOX2+ cells.
claims.source: Lineage tracing confirmed expression of membrane GFP in tumourigenic lesions, characterised by the accumulation of YAP and expansion of SOX2+ cells, suggesting they were solely derived from SOX2+ cells (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: LATS kinase activity is required to regulate the pituitary stem cell compartment.
claims.source: Taken together, our data support that LATS kinase activity is required to regulate the pituitary stem cell compartment.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LATS deletion experiments.

claims.claim: Loss of LATS1 is sufficient to drive deregulation of SOX2+ pituitary stem cells, generating highly proliferative non-functioning tumours with features of carcinomas.
claims.source: Loss of LATS1 is sufficient to drive deregulation of SOX2+ pituitary stem cells, generating highly proliferative non-functioning tumours with features of carcinomas.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LATS1 deletion experiments and tumour characterization.

claims.claim: No tumours were observed at any stage analysed in YAP-TetO animals treated with doxycycline from P21 to P105 (n = 12).
claims.source: We did not observe the formation of tumours at any stage analysed (n = 12, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the postnatal YAP-TetO experiments.

claims.claim: No lesions were observed in YAP-TetO animals when treating from P5.
claims.source: Similarly, we did not observe the formation of lesions when treating from P5.
claims.evidence: This is an observation from the postnatal YAP-TetO experiments.

claims.claim: Elevation of YAP protein levels was confirmed in YAP-TetO animals following three weeks of doxycycline treatment (P42), displaying patchy accumulation.
claims.source: Elevation of YAP protein levels was confirmed following three weeks of doxycycline treatment (P42), displaying patchy accumulation, likely a result of genetic recombination efficiencies (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: There was robust elevation in the expression of transcriptional targets Cyr61 and Ctgf in YAP-TetO animals following treatment.
claims.source: Consistent with pathway activation, there was robust elevation in the expression of transcriptional targets Cyr61 and Ctgf following treatment (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Target expression in YAP-TetO animals was at significantly lower levels compared to Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ deletions.
claims.source: however at significantly lower levels compared to Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ deletions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantified RNAscope data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: There was no elevation in phosphorylated inactive YAP in YAP-TetO animals.
claims.source: and there was no elevation in phosphorylated inactive YAP (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Immunofluorescence against SOX2 demonstrated a significant increase in the number of SOX2+ cells as a proportion of the anterior pituitary in YAP-TetO animals at P42 (18.0% compared to 12.1% in controls, p=0.0014).
claims.source: Immunofluorescence against SOX2 demonstrated a significant increase in the number of SOX2+ cells as a proportion of the anterior pituitary (Figure 5B,F; 18.0% compared to 12.1% in controls, p=0.0014)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B,F.

claims.claim: The increase in the percentage of SOX2+ cells in YAP-TetO animals was maintained at all stages analysed.
claims.source: This increase in the percentage of SOX2+ cells was maintained at all stages analysed (Figure 5F) and did not affect the overall morphology of the pituitary.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantified data shown in Figure 5F.

claims.claim: At P42, a significant increase in proliferation among the SOX2+ pituitary stem cells was observed in YAP-TetO animals, from 3% in controls to 15% in mutants (p=0.027).
claims.source: At P42 we observed a significant increase in proliferation among the SOX2+ pituitary stem cells from 3% in controls to 15% in mutants (p=0.027).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: SOX2+ cells make up 10% of all cycling cells (Ki-67+) in normal pituitaries, but this increased to 25% in YAP-TetO mutants.
claims.source: SOX2+ cells make up 10% of all cycling cells (Ki-67%) in normal pituitaries, however in mutants this increased to 25%, suggesting a preferential expansion of the SOX2+ population, rather than an overall increase in proliferation (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claims.claim: Longer treatment (P21 to P105) in YAP-TetO animals resulted in sporadic regions of expanded SOX2+ cells.
claims.source: No additional marked differences were observed in samples analysed at P63 (6 weeks of treatment, n = 3), however longer treatment (P21 to P105) resulted in sporadic regions of expanded SOX2+ cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Regions of expanded SOX2+ cells in YAP-TetO animals did not express the commitment marker PIT1.
claims.source: These regions did not express the commitment marker PIT1 and were identifiable by haematoxylin/eosin staining.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence and histological data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: In contrast to tumour lesions generated following loss of LATS kinases, regions of expanded SOX2+ cells in YAP-TetO animals were not proliferative, were positive for pYAP and did not accumulate high levels of YAP/TAZ (n = 6 lesions).
claims.source: In contrast to tumour lesions generated following loss of LATS kinases, these were not proliferative, were positive for pYAP and did not accumulate high levels of YAP/TAZ (n = 6 lesions).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: The sustained expression of constitutive active YAP can activate the proliferation of SOX2 stem cells, but in contrast to deletion of LATS1, this alone is not oncogenic.
claims.source: Together these results suggest that the sustained expression of constitutive active YAP can activate the proliferation of SOX2 stem cells, but in contrast to deletion of LATS1, this alone is not oncogenic.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing YAP-TetO and LATS deletion phenotypes.

claims.claim: Immunofluorescence against total YAP protein confirmed restoration of the normal YAP expression pattern and levels after recovery in YAP-TetO animals.
claims.source: Immunofluorescence against total YAP protein confirmed restoration of the normal YAP expression pattern and levels after recovery (Figure 5E)
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5E.

claims.claim: mRNA in situ hybridisation detected a reduction in expression of YAP/TAZ targets Cyr61 and Ctgf after recovery in YAP-TetO animals.
claims.source: and mRNA in situ hybridisation detected a reduction in expression of YAP/TAZ targets Cyr61 and Ctgf (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by RNAscope data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: Following recovery from high levels of YAP, the number of SOX2+ cells reduced to comparable levels as in controls (around 10% of the total anterior pituitary).
claims.source: Following recovery from high levels of YAP, the number of SOX2+ cells reduced to comparable levels as in controls (around 10% of the total anterior pituitary) (Figure 5E,F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by quantified immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5E,F.

claims.claim: The effects of YAP overexpression on the stem cell population are transient following three weeks of treatment.
claims.source: This suggests that the effects of YAP overexpression on the stem cell population are transient following three weeks of treatment (Figure 5F).
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the recovery experiments.

claims.claim: Larger clones of SOX2 derivatives were observed at P63 in Sox2CreERT2/+;R26rtTA/mTmG;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ animals compared to controls.
claims.source: Larger clones of SOX2 derivatives were observed at P63 in Sox2CreERT2/+;R26rtTA/mTmG;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ animals compared to controls, and these still contained SOX2+ cells (Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 5H.

claims.claim: GFP+ derivatives of SOX2+ cells were detected which had differentiated into the three lineages (PIT1, SF1 and ACTH) following withdrawal in Sox2CreERT2/+;R26rtTA/mTmG;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ animals.
claims.source: Following withdrawal, we were able to detect GFP+ derivatives of SOX2+ cells, which had differentiated into the three lineages (PIT1, SF1 and ACTH, marking corticotrophs of the TPIT lineage) (Figure 5I).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5I.

claims.claim: Sustained expression of YAP is sufficient to maintain the SOX2+ state and promote activation of normal SOX2+ pituitary stem cells in vivo, driving expansion of this population.
claims.source: Taken together, these findings confirm that sustained expression of YAP is sufficient to maintain the SOX2+ state and promote activation of normal SOX2+ pituitary stem cells in vivo, driving expansion of this population.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the YAP-TetO and lineage tracing experiments.

claims.claim: Regulation of LATS/YAP/TAZ signalling is essential during anterior pituitary development and can influence the activity of the stem/progenitor cell pool.
claims.source: Here we establish that regulation of LATS/YAP/TAZ signalling is essential during anterior pituitary development and can influence the activity of the stem/progenitor cell pool.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion from all the experimental data.

claims.claim: LATS kinases, mediated by YAP and TAZ, are responsible for controlling organ growth, promoting an undifferentiated state and repressing lineage commitment.
claims.source: LATS kinases, mediated by YAP and TAZ, are responsible for controlling organ growth, promoting an undifferentiated state and repressing lineage commitment.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the LATS deletion experiments.

claims.claim: Loss of both Lats1 and Lats2 leads to dramatic tissue overgrowth during gestation, revealing a function for these enzymes in restricting growth during pituitary development.
claims.source: Loss of both Lats1 and Lats2, encoding potent tumour suppressors, leads to dramatic tissue overgrowth during gestation, revealing a function for these enzymes in restricting growth during pituitary development.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the embryonic LATS1/2 deletion experiments.

claims.claim: The involvement of YAP/TAZ and dysfunction of the kinase cascade is emerging in multiple paediatric cancers, which are often developmental disorders.
claims.source: The involvement of YAP/TAZ and dysfunction of the kinase cascade is emerging in multiple paediatric cancers, which are often developmental disorders (Ahmed et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claims.claim: Loss of LATS1 heterozygosity has been reported in a range of human tumours.
claims.source: Loss of LATS1 heterozygosity has been reported in a range of human tumours (Lee et al., 1990; Chen et al., 2005; Theile et al., 1996; Mazurenko et al., 1999) leading to an increase in YAP/TAZ protein levels.

results.result: Sustained embryonic and postnatal YAP activation (YAP-TetO model) prevents lineage commitment, maintains SOX2+ progenitor state, and leads to formation of Rathke's cleft cyst-like structures. YAP-TetO embryos at 15.5dpc showed YAP accumulation, upregulation of target gene Cyr61, dysplastic anterior pituitary lacking a central lumen, abundant SOX2+ cells in lateral regions, and dramatic reduction in committed lineages (PIT1, TPIT, SF1). Postnatal YAP-TetO animals developed multiple anterior lobe cysts lined by SOX2+, cytokeratin+, p63+ cells with ciliated and mucous cell features resembling RCC.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C34 provide comprehensive experimental evidence from the YAP-TetO model including immunofluorescence, RNAscope, histology, and quantified lineage marker data (Figure 1 and supplements). The phenotypic characterization is thorough with appropriate controls, statistical analysis (Student's t-tests with significant p-values), and multiple complementary techniques demonstrating consistent effects of YAP overexpression on progenitor maintenance and cyst formation.

results.result: YAP/TAZ are not required for SOX2+ cell specification, survival, or lineage commitment during pituitary development. Hesx1Cre/+;Yapfl/fl;Taz-/- double mutants showed normal pituitary morphology at 13.5dpc and normal spatial distribution of SOX2+ cells at embryonic and postnatal stages (13.5dpc, 16.0dpc, P28), even in regions devoid of both TAZ and active YAP. Commitment markers PIT1, SF1, and ACTH showed no differences between mutants and controls.
results.evaluation: Claims C35-C40 demonstrate through loss-of-function experiments that YAP/TAZ deletion does not affect SOX2+ cell specification or lineage commitment. The data include histology, immunofluorescence at multiple developmental stages, and breeding data (Supplementary file 1). However, the conclusion (C40) that YAP functions to promote SOX2 cell identity appears to contradict the lack of phenotype in the deletion mutants, suggesting this interpretation may be overreaching from the gain-of-function data alone.

results.result: STK3/4 kinases are not critical for YAP/TAZ regulation in the pituitary. Conditional deletion of Stk3 and Stk4 in Hesx1Cre/+;Stk3fl/fl;Stk4fl/fl embryos resulted in >75% reduction in STK3/4 proteins but did not lead to pituitary phenotype. Mutant pituitaries were macroscopically normal at birth, showed normal YAP/TAZ expression patterns, normal lineage commitment at P10, and remained histologically normal until P70.
results.evaluation: Claims C41-C46 provide clear evidence through western blot quantification (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), immunofluorescence, and histology that STK3/4 deletion does not affect pituitary development despite substantial protein reduction. The conclusion (C46) that these kinases are not critical is well-supported, though the authors appropriately note that residual activity or alternative kinases may compensate.

results.result: LATS1/2 kinases are required for normal embryonic pituitary development, controlling organ size, SOX2+ progenitor proliferation, and lineage commitment. Single deletion of Lats1 showed compensatory Lats2 upregulation. Homozygous Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/fl mutants showed embryonic/perinatal lethality, dramatic overgrowth by 13.5dpc with YAP/TAZ accumulation and loss of pYAP-S127, highly proliferative SOX2+ cells (Ki-67 index 76% vs 47% in controls, p=0.0067), and severe reduction in committed lineages (PIT1, TPIT, SF1) at 15.5dpc. By 15.5dpc, mutants showed gross enlargement, cysts, necrosis, and poor vascularization.
results.evaluation: Claims C47-C64 provide comprehensive evidence for LATS1/2 function through multiple genetic approaches, quantified proliferation data, lineage marker quantification with statistical analysis, and RNAscope for compensatory mechanisms. The progression from single to double deletions demonstrates functional redundancy. The data consistently support that LATS kinases regulate YAP/TAZ to control progenitor proliferation and differentiation during embryonic development.

results.result: Postnatal loss of LATS1 (with or without Lats2 haploinsufficiency) results in non-secreting pituitary tumors with features of squamous carcinoma. By P56, all Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl pituitaries showed lesions with abnormal morphology. Hesx1Cre/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+ tumors appeared earlier (P10-P21) with 3-8 lesions per animal, characterized by frequent mitoses, focal necrosis, squamous differentiation, elevated Ki-67 (7-28%, mean 15.46% vs 2.97% controls, p=0.0217), YAP/TAZ accumulation, upregulated Cyr61/Ctgf, and composed of 85-97% SOX2+ cells. Tumors were positive for cytokeratins (AE1/AE3) and p63, but negative for neuroendocrine markers (synaptophysin, NSE, chromogranin A) and vimentin, with sparse lineage commitment markers and elevated DNA damage.
results.evaluation: Claims C65-C81 provide extensive histopathological characterization of postnatal LATS deletion tumors with quantified proliferation data, comprehensive immunohistochemistry panel, and statistical analysis. The characterization as squamous carcinoma is well-supported by the marker profile. The data demonstrate that LATS1 loss alone is sufficient for tumor formation, accelerated by Lats2 haploinsufficiency.

results.result: SOX2+ cells are the cell of origin of LATS-deficient pituitary tumors, demonstrated by lineage tracing. Tamoxifen induction at P5 or P21 in Sox2CreERT2/+;Lats1fl/fl;Lats2fl/+;R26mTmG/+ mice led to abnormal lesions within three months in all cases. Lesions showed YAP/TAZ accumulation, activated Cyr61/Ctgf expression, epithelial ruffling, lack of lineage commitment markers, and similar marker profile to Hesx1-Cre tumors (p63+, AE1/AE3+). Lineage tracing confirmed membrane GFP expression in tumorigenic lesions characterized by YAP accumulation and SOX2+ cell expansion.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C91 provide definitive lineage tracing evidence using the Sox2-CreERT2 system with mTmG reporter, demonstrating that SOX2+ cells give rise to tumors. The phenotypic similarity between Hesx1-Cre and Sox2-CreERT2 driven deletions, combined with GFP+ labeling of tumor cells, strongly supports SOX2+ cells as the cell of origin. This is a critical finding establishing stem cell transformation.

results.result: Postnatal YAP activation alone (YAP-TetO) expands SOX2+ stem cells without causing tumors. Treatment from P21-P105 (12 weeks) showed no tumor formation (n=12). At P42, YAP-TetO animals showed patchy YAP accumulation, elevated Cyr61/Ctgf (but significantly lower than LATS deletions), no pYAP elevation, significant increase in SOX2+ cells (18.0% vs 12.1%, p=0.0014), and increased SOX2+ proliferation (15% vs 3%, p=0.027). SOX2+ cells comprised 25% of cycling cells vs 10% in controls. Longer treatment (P105) resulted in sporadic SOX2+ expansions that were non-proliferative, pYAP+, and lacked high YAP/TAZ accumulation, contrasting with LATS deletion tumors.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C105 demonstrate through quantified immunofluorescence and RNAscope that YAP activation alone expands stem cells but is not oncogenic. The comparison with LATS deletion phenotypes (C96, C104) is critical, showing lower target gene activation and lack of tumor formation. Statistical analysis supports the stem cell expansion phenotype. This establishes a threshold model where YAP level determines outcome.

results.result: YAP-induced stem cell expansion is reversible and expanded cells retain differentiation capacity. After 3 weeks doxycycline treatment followed by 3 weeks withdrawal, YAP-TetO animals showed restoration of normal YAP expression, reduction in Cyr61/Ctgf, and return of SOX2+ cells to control levels (~10%). Lineage tracing in Sox2CreERT2/+;R26rtTA/mTmG;Col1a1tetO-Yap/+ animals showed larger clones at P63 that still contained SOX2+ cells, and following withdrawal, GFP+ derivatives differentiated into all three lineages (PIT1, SF1, ACTH).
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C112 provide strong evidence for reversibility through recovery experiments with appropriate controls and lineage tracing demonstrating differentiation capacity. The data show that YAP-expanded stem cells are not irreversibly transformed and can contribute to normal lineages, contrasting with LATS deletion. This is important for understanding the distinction between physiological stem cell activation and transformation.

results.result: The LATS/YAP/TAZ signaling cascade is essential for normal pituitary development, controlling organ size and lineage specification from SOX2+ progenitors. LATS kinases, mediated by YAP and TAZ, control organ growth, promote undifferentiated state, and repress lineage commitment. Loss of both Lats1 and Lats2 leads to dramatic tissue overgrowth during gestation.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C113-C115 are high-level summary conclusions well-supported by the comprehensive experimental data from embryonic YAP gain-of-function (C20-C34) and LATS loss-of-function experiments (C52-C64). The conclusions appropriately synthesize the developmental phenotypes observed across multiple genetic models.

results.result: The LATS/YAP/TAZ cascade regulates pituitary stem cells in normal physiology and tumourigenesis, where loss of LATS1 is sufficient to drive SOX2+ stem cell transformation into aggressive non-functioning tumors. The phenotype is accelerated by additional Lats2 deletion and occurs whether deletions are performed embryonically or postnatally. Fine-tuning of pathway expression determines whether stem cells undergo physiological reactivation or tumourigenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C6, C90, C91, C120-C122, C144-C145 represent the central conclusions of the manuscript, well-supported by the comprehensive genetic, histological, and lineage tracing data. The distinction between YAP activation (stem cell expansion) and LATS deletion (tumourigenesis) supports the threshold/fine-tuning model. The data consistently demonstrate transformation of SOX2+ cells into carcinoma-like tumors.

results.result: Sustained YAP expression alone expands SOX2+ stem cells capable of differentiation without tumourigenic potential. YAP activation pushes stem cells into an activated state with expanded proliferative capacity but does not fully recapitulate LATS deletion phenotypes or lead to tumor formation during 12 weeks of activation. YAP has an isolated role in promoting stem cell pool expansion and restoring proliferative potential.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C105, C112, C134, C136, C139 synthesize the YAP gain-of-function results, distinguishing them from LATS deletion. The conclusions are well-supported by the experimental data showing stem cell expansion without transformation, reversibility, and retained differentiation capacity. This establishes YAP's specific role in stem cell activation distinct from its role in tumourigenesis when LATS is lost.

results.result: Target gene elevation is lower in YAP-TetO pituitaries compared to LATS1/2 deletions, suggesting signaling levels are critical for progression from cysts to tumors, and that tumourigenesis may be associated with signaling levels rising above a threshold.
results.evaluation: Claims C128 and C137 are supported by quantified RNAscope data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E) showing significantly different Cyr61/Ctgf expression levels between models. The threshold hypothesis is reasonable speculation based on the dose-response relationship observed, though it remains a hypothesis requiring further testing. The data support that signaling intensity correlates with phenotypic severity.

results.result: The tumors generated in LATS1/2 mouse models fit the histopathological profile of human pituitary carcinomas, and genetic lineage tracing identified SOX2+ cells as the cell of origin, with potential implications for human pituitary tumors composed of uncommitted cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C129-C130 are supported by comprehensive histopathological characterization (C69-C79) showing features consistent with carcinoma and definitive lineage tracing data (C82-C91). The comparison to human pituitary carcinomas is reasonable based on the marker profile, though the claim about implications for human disease is speculative and would require validation in human samples.

results.result: Background and context claims establishing prior knowledge about pituitary stem cells, anatomy, development, tumors, and the Hippo pathway. These include that SOX2+ PSCs persist throughout life and give rise to endocrine lineages, the pituitary structure and development, pituitary tumor epidemiology, Hippo pathway function in other organs, and previous observations of YAP/TAZ in pituitary stem cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C19 are background claims supported by appropriate citations to previous literature and established knowledge. These provide necessary context for the current work. The authors' previous work (C2, C18, C19) is appropriately cited and provides the foundation for the current investigation.

results.result: Discussion claims contextualizing findings within broader cancer biology and stem cell literature, including YAP/TAZ involvement in pediatric cancers, LATS1 loss in human tumors, previous Lats1 deletion studies, alternative LATS regulation mechanisms, squamous cell carcinoma reports, SOX2-YAP interactions in other cancers, YAP's role in stem cells in other tissues, temporal control in tumor models, YAP/TAZ regulation by tissue density and crosstalk with Notch signaling.
results.evaluation: Claims C116-C143 are discussion points appropriately supported by citations to relevant literature. These contextualize the findings within the broader field and propose mechanisms, though some represent speculation about mechanisms (C123, C137) or potential clinical relevance that would require further validation.

results.result: Summary and translational claims including that tumors are composed of SOX2+ cells with squamous differentiation, YAP-TetO model develops RCC-like cysts, YAP/TAZ likely function in positive feedback with SOX2 to maintain stem state and inhibit differentiation, and findings may aid treatment design and regenerative medicine approaches.
results.evaluation: Claims C125 and C127 are well-supported summaries of experimental data. Claim C133 about positive feedback with SOX2 is reasonable speculation based on the data and literature but lacks direct experimental evidence in this system. Claim C146 about clinical applications is aspirational and speculative, representing potential future directions rather than demonstrated utility.
